title: Amazon DynamoDB for Applications

header.html: Configure DynamoDB to support applications: high-cardinality partition keys, read consistency models, query and scan operations, keys, attributes and indexes (1.3.4)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 1.3

html:
1The data model

Amazon DynamoDB is a managed, serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit-millisecond latency.

Term Meaning
Table A collection of items
Item One record (up to 400 KB)
Attribute A field; items in a table need not share attributes
Partition key Decides which partition stores the item; required
Sort key Optional; items with the same partition key are ordered by it
Primary key The partition key, or partition key + sort key

Choosing keys

A good partition key is high-cardinality (many distinct values) so requests spread evenly. A hot partition happens when one key gets most of the traffic (a date, a status flag, a popular item).

Exam tip

. "Uneven load on one partition" = choose a higher-cardinality partition key, or add a suffix to spread writes.

2Reading data

Operation What it does Cost
GetItem One item by full primary key Cheapest
Query Items with one partition key value, optionally a sort key condition Efficient
Scan Reads the whole table Expensive; a filter expression applies after the read, so you still pay for all items scanned

Use projection expressions to return only some attributes, and handle pagination with LastEvaluatedKey.

Read consistency

Model Behavior
Eventually consistent (default) May return slightly stale data; half the cost
Strongly consistent Returns the latest write; costs more; not available on global secondary indexes
Transactional All-or-nothing reads and writes across items (higher cost)

3Capacity

Mode Use
On-demand Unpredictable traffic; pay per request
Provisioned Predictable traffic; set read and write capacity units, optional auto scaling

One read capacity unit (RCU) = one strongly consistent read up to 4 KB per second (or two eventually consistent). One write capacity unit (WCU) = one write up to 1 KB per second. If you exceed capacity you get ProvisionedThroughputExceededException: retry with backoff. [Verify live]

4Indexes and other features

Feature Meaning
Local secondary index (LSI) Same partition key, different sort key; created with the table only
Global secondary index (GSI) Any partition and sort key; has its own capacity; eventually consistent only
Conditional writes Write only if a condition holds; implements optimistic locking
TTL Automatically delete expired items by a timestamp attribute (Module 7)
Streams Ordered change records, read by Lambda
DAX In-memory cache in front of DynamoDB (Module 15)
Batch and transactions BatchGetItem and BatchWriteItem (up to 100 reads and 25 writes); TransactWriteItems for all-or-nothing
Exam tip

. Eventually consistent reads cost half; strongly consistent reads are not available on a global secondary index.

Exam tip

. Query and GetItem are the efficient reads; Scan reads the whole table and a filter expression does not reduce the capacity you pay for.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A table uses "order date" as the partition key and all writes go to today's value. What is the problem?

  • AToo many indexes
  • BMissing TTL
  • CA hot partition
  • DRead consistency
Show the answer

Answer: C. A low-cardinality, time-based key concentrates writes on one partition.

S2A developer must look up all orders of one customer, newest first. Which design fits?

  • AScan the whole table and filter the results by customer in the application
  • BA random partition key so that the orders are spread across partitions
  • CPartition key CustomerId and sort key OrderDate, then Query
  • DA single global item that contains every order as a list attribute
Show the answer

Answer: C. Query on a partition key with a sort key returns related items in order efficiently.

S3An application needs the latest data right after a write. Which read mode should it use?

  • AEventually consistent
  • BStrongly consistent on the table
  • CStrongly consistent on a global secondary index
  • DScan with a filter
Show the answer

Answer: B. Strongly consistent reads return the latest write, but not on a GSI.

S4A team must query the table by an attribute that is not part of its key. What is the best option?

  • AA full table scan every time with a filter expression on that attribute
  • BA global secondary index on that attribute
  • CA larger item size so that the attribute can be read faster
  • DA second Region with a replica of the table for the lookups
Show the answer

Answer: B. A GSI provides an alternate key for queries.

S5Two clients update the same item and one overwrites the other. How can the developer detect this?

  • ATTL on a timestamp attribute so that stale writes expire
  • BA scan before each write to compare the current contents
  • CA larger read capacity so that clients see each other's writes
  • DA conditional write using a version attribute
Show the answer

Answer: D. Conditional writes implement optimistic locking.

S6An application has unpredictable traffic and the team wants no capacity planning. Which capacity mode fits?

  • AProvisioned
  • BReserved
  • COn-demand
  • DBurst-only
Show the answer

Answer: C. On-demand scales automatically and bills per request.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the maximum item size?

Show the answer

400 KB.

R2Which is cheaper, Query or Scan?

Show the answer

Query.

R3What does one RCU provide?

Show the answer

One strongly consistent read of up to 4 KB per second (or two eventually consistent reads).

R4Which index type must be created with the table?

Show the answer

A local secondary index.

R5Can a GSI serve strongly consistent reads?

Show the answer

No, only eventually consistent.

R6What does a conditional write enable?

Show the answer

Optimistic locking and safe updates.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Keys partition (+ sort); high cardinality avoids hot partitions
Reads GetItem, Query (efficient), Scan (whole table, filter after)
Consistency eventual (default, cheaper), strong (not on GSI), transactional
Capacity on-demand vs provisioned; RCU 4 KB, WCU 1 KB
Indexes LSI (table creation, same partition key), GSI (any key, eventual)
